summary: Elevated first-byte latency on chat completions after runtime hotpatch and LB affinity change
description:
Issue summary:
StreamlineAI reports a persistent elevation in 'time-to-first-byte' (first token emitted) for chat completion requests after our runtime hotpatch (2026-03-11) and a load-balancer affinity change that rolled out the same morning. Impact is concentrated on their dedicated cluster in us-west-1 using rw-3.1-large (and the quantized variant).

Impact:
- P95 first-byte latency increased from ~120ms to ~540ms for short chat prompts (<=64 tokens).
- Customers observed occasional 30s client-side timeouts when initial token emission exceeded client thresholds.
- Affects ~12% of requests for the customer during peak (09:00-11:00 PST).

Environment:
- Customer: StreamlineAI (dedicated reservation)
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-1)
- Models: rw-3.1-large (primary), rw-3.1-quantized (fallback)
- Runtime: rtx-runtime-2.1.7 -> hotpatched to rtx-runtime-2.1.8 on 2026-03-11 03:22 UTC
- LB config: affinity change (session stickiness tweak) rolled out 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use StreamlineAI account with dedicated pool and send 1k short chat requests (prompt length 10-40 tokens) at concurrency 20 from us-west region.
2) Observe latency distribution and connection logs.
3) Compare first-byte timings against baseline from 2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent but repeatable stalls between connection handshake and first token emission.
- Traces show increased time inside serving-runtime on 'KV cache miss + kernel selection' path for affected requests.
- Affected requests frequently land on a subset of hosts that show CPU spin waiting on a kernel JIT/compat check.

Expected behavior:
- First token emitted within 100-200ms for short prompts under dedicated SLA.

Logs & metrics links:
- Grafana (customer p95 first-byte): https://grafana.internal.redwood/a/graphs/streamlineai/first-byte?from=2026-03-10&to=2026-03-13
- Traces: https://jaeger.internal.redwood/trace/7a8f3c2a
- LB rollout audit: https://infra.redwood/audit/logs/2026-03-11/lb-affinity
investigation_notes:
Timeline and quick findings:
- 2026-03-11 03:22 UTC: rtx-runtime-2.1.8 hotpatch deployed cluster-wide (cherry-picked quant path fix).
- 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC: Load-balancer stickiness tweak rolled (goal: reduce cross-AZ tail latency).
- 03/11 04:15 UTC: StreamlineAI support ticket opened reporting spikes.

Hypotheses tested so far:
1) Kernel selection/quant path regression in 2.1.8: reproduced increased per-request setup time in staging with 2.1.8 when model variant uses quantized kernels.
2) LB affinity change concentrating traffic on a smaller hot pool exposing cold-Warmed worker state: correlation observed — affected hosts had higher number of cold model instantiations per minute.
3) KV cache priming race with new runtime path: traces show ~70ms extra spent waiting for KV cache population on misses when requests hit a recently-started process.

Findings:
- Canary tests show that mixing affinity change + runtime 2.1.8 increases probability of a request landing on a cold host (no warmed KV) by ~3x relative to previous setup.
- Those cold hosts take extra ~300-450ms before first token while JIT/compat checks and cache priming run.
- Rolling back LB affinity on a small subset reduced first-byte p95 back toward baseline for that slice.

Next immediate actions:
- Scoped rollback of LB affinity tweak for StreamlineAI dedicated pool (in progress).
- Scheduling a rollback of runtime hotpatch 2.1.8 on affected dedicated pools if rollback of LB affinity does not restore baseline in 30m.
- Instrument additional telemetry in kernel-selection path to capture precise JIT/cold-init counts (PR opened).
comments: [2026-03-12 09:14 UTC] Lena Park (Support): Customer alerted that after morning deploy they observed a 4-5x increase in p95 first-token latency. They provided example request IDs and SDK logs. Attaching logs to ticket.

[2026-03-12 09:48 UTC] Priya Singh (SRE): Started correlation of host-level metrics. Noted subset of nodes with elevated 'model-initialization' time and high counts of 'kernel-compat-check' events. Marked nodes for deeper inspection.

[2026-03-12 10:05 UTC] Diego Morales (Serving Runtime): Reproduced locally with 2.1.8 + affinity change. Observed extra setup time from a new compat check path introduced to handle quantized kernels. Created PR to gate compat checks behind warmed-cache flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

[2026-03-12 10:42 UTC] Lena Park (Support) -> StreamlineAI: Provided guidance to temporarily pin their workload to rw-3.1-large on runtime rtx-runtime-2.1.7. Customer agreed to test a routing pin for a 30-minute window and report results.
[2026-03-13 02:17 UTC] StreamlineAI (customer comment): After pinning to 2.1.7 first-byte p95 dropped back to ~140ms. Observed ~95% of requests within SLA now. Still seeing a few outliers.

[2026-03-14 08:22 UTC] Priya Singh (SRE): Rolling back LB affinity in StreamlineAI's dedicated pool as an intermediate mitigation. Monitoring metrics; will follow up with a plan for either full runtime rollback or a targeted runtime fix.
workaround: Temporary workaround provided to customer: pin their routing to runtime rtx-runtime-2.1.7 (pre-hotpatch) or route to rw-3.1-large on a warmed pool. Support created a routing pin for StreamlineAI and verified improvement within 20 minutes.
resolution_plan: Short-term: keep LB affinity rollback in place for StreamlineAI and monitor for 24 hours. If metrics remain stable, schedule a targeted runtime patch that removes the opportunistic compat/JIT check on cold hosts (PR #4321).\nLong-term: add startup warmup to dedicated pools during scale-up to ensure KV cache priming and kernel warm paths are executed before accepting steady traffic. Add gating for new compat checks behind an opt-in flag for dedicated customers.
